title: Teen numbers: 10 and some more
examples: How do I know when to make a group of ten?
What does it mean to have ten and some more?
Can we count past ten using rods?

explain.say: Today we are learning about numbers bigger than ten. We will learn to group things into tens. This helps us count much faster.
Look here. We have ten fingers on two hands. This is one full group of ten. We can use rods to show this group.
If we have one ten group and four single rods, we have fourteen. So, ten plus four equals fourteen.

items: One ten group and four single rods

explain.say: Let us try another one. If we have two ten groups and three single rods, we have twenty-three. This shows 23.

faq.a: A ten group is just ten things put together. It is a neat way to count ten items.
asks: What does it mean to group by ten?
How many things are in one ten group?

faq.q: Why do we use rods to show tens?
faq.a: We use rods because they help us see the pattern of ten. It keeps our counting organized.
asks: Are rods just for showing ten?
Why can't we just count them normally?

faq.q: How do I show the number seventeen?
faq.a: You show it as one group of ten and seven single rods. That is ten and seven.
asks: What is 17 in tens and ones?
Can you show me seventeen with rods?

faq.q: Is ten plus five always fifteen?
faq.a: Yes, ten plus five always equals fifteen. You just count on from ten.
asks: If I have ten and five more, what is it?
Does ten plus five equal fifteen?

faq.q: What is the difference between ten and one?
faq.a: Ten is a full group of ten things. One is just a single item by itself.
asks: What is the difference between 10 and 1?
When do I use a ten rod versus a single rod?

facts: A ten group always contains exactly ten items.
When counting, we count the full tens first, then the ones.
Ten plus any number is just counting up from ten.
The number eleven is one ten group and one single rod.

quiz.say: If you have two ten rods and five single rods, what number is that?
quiz.why: You have two full groups of ten, which is twenty. Then you add the five single rods to get twenty-five.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you add the number of rods together instead of grouping them.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only count the tens and ignore the extra ones.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you only count the full groups of ten and forget the single ones.

quiz.say: Show the number nineteen using tens and ones.
quiz.why: Nineteen has one full group of ten, and there are nine single rods left over.

wrong.0: This is correct, but the best way to show it is by describing the rods.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you only count the first number you see.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you count the number of rods incorrectly.

quiz.why: When you start at ten and count up six more, you land exactly on sixteen.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you multiply ten by six instead of adding.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you put the numbers next to each other without adding.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you only count the tens and forget the extra six.
